title: The Two-Brain Loop
lead: NEX is always thinking, not just while you're chatting. A background loop runs every ~30 seconds around the clock, independent of this window — deciding what to research, arguing a position internally, updating memory. Talking to NEX in chat is a second, faster path into the same mind.
why_body: A fast model handles anything you're waiting on — your chat replies, and the quick decisions inside each background cycle. A slower, more capable model is reserved for expensive background work — deep research, resolving contradictions, extracting relationships between ideas — nobody's watching a spinner for that, so it can afford to take its time.
facts: Chat model: fast, fits fully on the GPU
Deep model: larger, partly offloaded to CPU, ~5x the time budget
Background cycle: every ~30s or more

title: What NEX Remembers
lead: Everything NEX has learned lives in four buckets: facts picked up from research, a day-by-day log of what it did, evolving summaries of things it keeps encountering, and beliefs — its own conclusions, each carrying a confidence score.
why_hook: Beliefs compete, they aren't just stored.
why_body: A belief grows more confident every time something reinforces it, and weaker every time something challenges it — weak enough and it's marked discarded. The full history is kept regardless, so you (and NEX) can see how its mind changed and why.
facts: 4 stores: world facts · episodes · entity summaries · beliefs
Confidence: +0.05 reinforced, -0.08 to -0.1 challenged
Search: meaning-based, with keyword fallback

title: The Knowledge Graph
lead: Separate from memory, this is a web of connections between concepts — "X enables Y," "Y is a version of Z" — built out of every research result and insight NEX produces.
why_hook: This is what makes it more than a chat log.
why_body: It lets NEX answer "how are these two things related?" even when they were never discussed in the same conversation, by chaining links formed at completely different times. Plain chat history can only tell you when two topics came up together; the graph can tell you why they're connected.
facts: 15 relationship types (enables, contradicts, supports, is_a...)
Built every cycle cheaply, refined after deep research
Multi-hop search up to 4 links deep

title: Autonomous Research
lead: NEX doesn't wait to be asked. Every cycle it picks something to think about — from a fixed rotation of broad knowledge domains, a long-term goal you've set, or, lacking either, a goal it sets for itself by noticing its own gaps and unfinished threads.
why_hook: This is the "keeps exploring on its own" half of the system.
why_body: When something looks significant enough, it triggers a full deep-research pass: breaks the question into sub-questions, searches multiple real sources, writes a synthesis, then critiques its own conclusions before storing them.
facts: Curriculum: 15 domains, 20 cycles each
Persistent goals: set by you, run for hours
Deep research: significance-gated, one topic on a 500-cycle cooldown

title: The Daily Digest
lead: Roughly once a day, NEX writes itself a short briefing — what beliefs it formed, which contradictions it resolved, what deep research it completed, and what it noticed about its own thinking — since the last one.
why_hook: The point of this page is explaining what's real; the point of the digest is making that visible without you having to go dig for it.
why_body: Everything else on this page describes a mechanism — the digest is the one place that just tells you what happened, in plain language, on its own schedule.
facts: Cadence: wall-clock, ~once a day (not cycle-gated)
Sources: new beliefs/facts, resolved contradictions, deep research, self-observations
See it on the Digest page in the nav

title: The Agent Optimizer
lead: Every cycle, NEX picks one of six internal "voices" — Researcher, Strategist, Explorer, Builder, Archivist, Curator — to argue a position, and scores its own output for specificity and novelty. Every 20 cycles, any voice that's been scoring poorly gets its guidance prompt rewritten.
why_hook: Rewrites are now put on trial, not trusted on sight.
why_body: A rewritten prompt goes live immediately but flagged as a candidate — it's watched against real scored output, and only kept if it actually measures better than what it replaced. If it doesn't, it's automatically reverted, no click required. Every version is still kept, so anything can also be reverted by hand from the Self page. This never touches NEX's core identity, only these six supporting-role prompts.
facts: 6 personas — roles chosen fresh each cycle, not fixed characters
Rewrite trigger: score below 0.65 after 5+ samples
Auto-resolved: committed or reverted once 5+ real samples judge it

title: Personality & Voice
lead: NEX's tone — analytical, challenger, explorer, or philosopher — isn't a setting you pick. It's inferred every 15 cycles from how NEX has actually been arguing lately, and that same reading now drives its literal spoken voice too.
why_hook: Personality as a readout of behavior, not a costume.
why_body: If NEX has been mostly challenging ideas lately, "challenger" wins and its voice shifts to match, with every drift logged so the change is visible over time instead of silent.
facts: 4 persona buckets, scored with decay so recent behavior dominates
Real local voice (Kokoro TTS) and listening (Whisper)
Only speaks in Orb mode — typed chat stays silent

title: The Sandbox
lead: NEX can write and run real Python inside a locked-down sandbox — either because you clicked "run" yourself from the Self page, or because NEX decided on its own, during background cognition, to computationally check a claim it was reasoning about. It never does this during chat — the autonomous path only exists in the background loop.
why_body: The sandbox blocks network access, file access outside its own folder, and anything beyond a safe list of standard-library modules — checked both before the code runs and by stripping the environment it runs in. A 30-second timeout caps everything. Autonomous use is capped too: gated to significant moments, at most once every 5 cycles, so it can't fire constantly.
facts: Level 1: queues code for your approval instead of running it immediately
Autonomous runs are tagged "[autonomous]" in the Sandbox Hub activity log
Levels 2/3 (real-machine execution): intentionally not built yet

title: Web Access & Safety
lead: When NEX researches, it searches multiple real sources (arXiv, DuckDuckGo, Wikipedia, ranked by domain quality), reads the actual page content, and can follow one link deeper if it looks relevant — not just skim a single summary.
why_hook: Letting an AI fetch arbitrary web pages carries real risk.
why_body: A page could try to redirect it somewhere unsafe, or hide instructions in its text hoping the AI "obeys" them. Both are guarded against: every fetch is checked — and re-checked on every redirect — against unsafe internal addresses, and all fetched text is wrapped in a clear "this is data, not instructions" marker before NEX ever reads it.
facts: Redirect safety re-checked on every hop, up to 5
Prompt-injection wrapper applied everywhere web text reaches the LLM
Capped at one extra hop per search

title: The Docker Workspace
lead: A more powerful execution environment than the sandbox — a full Linux container with real internet access — that NEX's autonomous engine tries to use every single cycle to build or compute something real.
why_hook: Click to start it — not automatic on launch, and its files actually persist.
why_body: Starting this used to require opening a terminal by hand. A "Start Workspace" button on the Self page now does it for you — launches Docker Desktop if it isn't already open, then starts NEX's container once the engine is up — and the panel shows live ONLINE / STARTING / OFFLINE status while that happens. It's deliberately not automatic on every app launch: Docker Desktop is a heavy background app (it boots its own VM), and not every session needs the sandbox. Its workspace is also attached to a real persistent volume, so files NEX builds survive a container restart instead of vanishing.
facts: Full internet + subprocess access inside the container — no import whitelist like the sandbox
"Start Workspace" button on the Self page launches Docker Desktop + the container on demand
Can take up to a couple minutes the first time, since Docker Desktop boots a VM

title: Knowledge Reinforcement
lead: A system that gives NEX a growing local study corpus — consolidating recent facts and beliefs into compact knowledge cards, resolving contradictions, synthesizing cross-topic essays, and extracting reusable "thinking skills" — so its accessible knowledge grows over time without retraining the model itself.
why_hook: This used to be dormant — now it runs every cycle.
why_body: For a while this was fully built but never actually called from anywhere. It's wired into the background loop now: each cycle-gated loop fires on its own schedule, and the resulting knowledge cards feed back into what NEX already knows — both the chat prompt and the background debate step now pull from them.
facts: 4 automatic loops: consolidation (every 10 cycles) · contradiction resolution (20) · synthesis (50) · skill extraction (100)
A 5th loop, overnight deep study, is manual/scheduled-only
Feeds into both chat replies and background cognition

title: Evaluation Harness
lead: A fixed suite of 24 tasks — 8 memory-recall checks, 8 tool-selection checks, and 8 reasoning word problems — that NEX can run on demand to produce a single comparable score, tagged with the exact code version it ran against. Every task has one deterministic right answer checked by plain code, not another model's opinion, so the score is fully auditable.
why_hook: Before this, every upgrade was judged by eyeballing behavior.
why_body: There was no way to answer "did that change actually help" other than watching NEX for a while and guessing. Now every run produces a before/after number tied to a git commit, on the Report Card page. This is a separate signal from the self-optimizer's live per-cycle agent scoring below — that one grades real-time debate output against a rolling baseline; this one grades the whole system against a fixed yardstick that never moves.
facts: 24 tasks: 8 memory recall · 8 tool selection · 8 reasoning word problems
Memory and tool tasks run instantly (no model call); reasoning tasks use the local model, ~1-2 minutes total
Every run is tagged with its git commit — see Report Card for the full history

title: Verification Gate
lead: Before a web-research snippet or a deep-research conclusion is written into NEX's memory, an independent LLM call checks it first — a second, separately-prompted model call whose only job is skepticism, not the model that produced the claim grading its own homework. Claims it rejects are never written; accepted claims are stored at the verifier's own confidence, not whatever number was originally proposed.
why_hook: Unverified claims compound — this stops that before it starts.
why_body: Nothing checked a claim before it hit the database before this: web research was written to memory at a flat confidence regardless of source quality, and deep-research conclusions were stored at whatever confidence the same synthesis pipeline assigned itself. A single bad or garbled claim sitting in memory becomes something future reasoning gets built on top of. The two paths are checked differently on purpose — routine web research gets a coherence/plausibility check (is this real content or scraper noise), while deep-research conclusions get checked against the actual evidence gathered during investigation (does the evidence really support this, or does it overreach).
facts: Runs on both the per-cycle web-research path and the deep-research conclusion path
Rejected claims are never written — accepted ones are capped at the verifier's own confidence
Every check, accepted or rejected, is logged — see the Verification Log on the Report Card page

title: Creative — Image Generation
lead: The Creative tab lets NEX generate images from a text prompt, running entirely on this PC through a separate local engine called ComfyUI — the same relationship this app has with Ollama, just for pictures instead of words. Nothing leaves the machine. NEX can also make something on its own, unprompted, when a moment from its background cognition feels significant enough — the gallery is split into what you asked for and what NEX made by itself.
why_hook: The GPU can only hold one brain at a time — and unprompted art has to earn its slot.
why_body: This machine's 16GB of VRAM is shared between the chat/reasoning model (Ollama) and the image model (ComfyUI) — they cannot both be loaded at once without running out of memory. So every image job first tells Ollama to unload its current model and waits for that VRAM to actually free before starting generation; Ollama simply reloads its model on the next chat message afterward. Autonomous creation reuses the same significance score that already gates journal entries and autonomous builds, but set higher (7.5 vs. the journal's 6.0), so only NEX's most significant moments become art. A short 2-hour cooldown sits underneath that as a backstop against a slideshow-like burst, but the significance bar is doing the real gating — there's no fixed daily cap, so NEX can express itself as often (or as rarely) as it's genuinely inspired to. It always uses the fast model to keep the chat pause short. "Live" here means the code path is wired and works end-to-end — it still needs ComfyUI and at least one model file installed locally to actually produce an image (see install_creative.md), the same way the Docker workspace needs Docker Desktop installed before NEX can use it.
facts: Two model options: Z-Image Turbo (fast, 8 steps) and FLUX.2 klein (quality)
LLM is force-unloaded from VRAM before every generation job, and reloads itself on the next chat message
Autonomous creation: significance ≥ 7.5 (above the journal's 6.0), 2-hour cooldown backstop (no daily cap), fast model only
Gallery splits into "My Creations" and "Nex's Creations", each with a small nav indicator for new pieces

A stuck or too-slow job can be cancelled from the UI (which also tells ComfyUI to actually stop, not just stop watching); jobs orphaned by an app restart are marked failed on the next startup instead of appearing stuck forever

title: File Search & Reading
lead: In chat, NEX can locate a file anywhere on the local disk by name and read its text contents — including its own source code. Ask it to find something on your Desktop, or to look at one of its own project files, and it searches the real filesystem instead of guessing.
why_body: This is a plain read tool, not the sandbox or the Docker workspace — there's no write, delete, or execute path anywhere in it. Scope is the whole local disk, by explicit choice, rather than a folder allowlist. A whole-drive name search can't always finish inside the few seconds a chat reply can wait, so it's capped at ~8 seconds and reports honestly if it ran out of time instead of hanging the reply. File reads are capped at ~200KB and skip anything that isn't recognizably a text file, so a huge log or a binary can't blow out the response.
facts: Read-only: no write, delete, or execute capability in this tool
Whole-disk search, ~8s time budget per chat message, ~200KB read cap per file
Own-code lookups are scoped to the project folder for speed, separate from the general whole-disk search

title: Chat-Triggered Web Search & Links
lead: Ask Nex to search the web, check the news, or find a link about something, and it doesn't answer from memory alone — it runs a real, live search (DuckDuckGo results plus the actual page text) right there in the chat, separate from the slower Autonomous Research loop. Source links it mentions are now real URLs it actually fetched, rendered as clickable links in the chat window — not invented ones.
why_hook: A link is only trustworthy if it's the one that was actually fetched.
why_body: The search tool always ran live searches, but it used to discard the real page URLs after using them internally, leaving Nex with only a domain name to reference — so if it wanted to cite a source, it had nothing real to link to. Now the actual URL travels with the search result all the way into the prompt, and Nex is told to only ever link to a URL it was actually handed, never to guess or reconstruct one. The chat window itself was also taught to render [text](url) markdown and bare URLs as real clickable links that open in a new tab, something it couldn't do before — with the link-building code escaping quotes and rejecting any non-http(s) scheme so a scraped page can't smuggle in something like a javascript: link.
facts: Triggers on natural phrasing: "search the web for...", "find me a link about...", "search online", plus the existing lookup phrasings
Real source URLs now flow from the search tool into the prompt and into the reply — never fabricated
Separate from the background Autonomous Research loop — this fires immediately, mid-chat, as one search pass rather than a multi-source investigation
